validity.recommendation: Cluster-level adjudication: compare P7818 (+ P7817) against P5989 'Taganrog-Melitopol-Berdyansk Gas Pipeline' (OtherEnglishNames 'Taganrog-Melitopol Gas Pipeline'; Status=operating since StartYear1=2024, ConstructionYear=2023/7, corridor Taganrog->Melitopol, straight-line 272.73 km). P5989's own sources describe modernization ('replacement of pipe... doubled pressure, 1.5x volume') of the SAME Taganrog-through-DNR corridor that P7817/P7818 track as a separate 'reconstruction of the retired Soviet Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk pipeline.' Independent UA source united24media.com (Jul 2025) describes 'two pipelines' being built along this stretch -- one Taganrog-Mariupol, another continuing to Berdyansk with Melitopol as the final destination -- which is consistent with P5989 being the SAME physical corridor as P7817+P7818 combined, just tracked under a different name/PID with a different (earlier, 'operating') status. Do not merge unilaterally -- flag for adjudication whether P5989 and P7817/P7818 are the same asset double-counted, or genuinely parallel/successive builds (e.g., P5989 = a faster interim pipe, P7817/P7818 = the slower Soviet-line capital-repair program).
validity.researcher_notes: GGIT gas sheet has FOUR rows on this exact geography: P1457 'Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk Gas Pipeline' (retired 2009, dia 1000mm, 516.00 km merged -- this is the original Soviet trunk, matches the gem.wiki infobox for Rostov-Taganrog-Zhdanov). P7817 = its Taganrog-Mariupol reconstruction (construction, 700mm). P7818 (this row) = its Mariupol-Berdyansk reconstruction (proposed, 500mm). P5989 = 'Taganrog-Melitopol-Berdyansk Gas Pipeline' (operating since 2024, no diameter recorded, sourced to TASS 2024-04-29 (tass.ru/obschestvo/20680005 -- 403'd for me directly but content recovered via web search snippet: 'В ДНР впервые не ограничивали потребление газа зимой' -- modernization of the Taganrog-Melitopol section THROUGH DNR, new pipe-laying doubled pressure/1.5x volume, now also supplies gas to Zaporizhzhia) and dan-news.ru 2023-07-27 (verified live, confirms only the two endpoints Taganrog/Melitopol, no diameter/length, no mention of Mariupol or Berdyansk in that specific article). Neither P5989 citation names Mariupol or Berdyansk explicitly, so I cannot mechanically prove P5989 IS the same pipe as P7817/P7818 -- but the geography (Taganrog->Melitopol necessarily transits the Mariupol/Berdyansk coastal corridor) and the independent United24 description of parallel construction along that exact stretch make this a real, non-trivial overlap risk, not a stretch. This is exactly the kind of relabeled/duplicate risk the sweep is designed to catch -- flagging rather than resolving per instructions.

validity.recommendation: Note the scope gap in ResearcherNotes: the sole citation for this row's Status/Diameter documents planning approval for only a 0.3 km repair stretch, not the full 68.93 km LengthEstimateKm. Do not change LengthEstimateKm without independent confirmation of the full-route scope.
validity.researcher_notes: Read the underlying primary document behind the sheet's own Status/Diameter [ref] (archive.org/details/58_20251012 = DNR Ministry of Construction Order No.58-od, 27.03.2025, full OCR text pulled from the item's own djvu.txt derivative). It approves territorial-planning documentation for THREE separate 'kapitalny remont' (capital repair, method = pipe replacement) linear objects: (1) Taganrog-Mariupol Дu700, km 29.0-71.625; (2) an internal Mariupol GRS-1-to-GRS-2 line, Дu700/500, km 0-11.815; and (3) 'Mariupol-Berdyansk Дu500 na uchastke km 0 - km 0.3' -- i.e. THIS row's own citation supports a capital-repair proposal for only the FIRST 300 METERS of the Mariupol-Berdyansk line, not a 68.93 km reconstruction. The underlying planning documentation was originally approved back on 29.05.2020 (pre-invasion; DNR evidently held provisional plans for this corridor years before Russia occupied Mariupol/Berdyansk in 2022) and the 2025 order is a re-confirmation/republication of that 2020 documentation. Diameter=500mm is well-supported (matches 'Дu500' exactly). Status=proposed is a defensible READING of 'documentation approved, repair not yet executed,' but LengthEstimateKm=68.93 (an unsourced straight-line Mariupol-Berdyansk city-distance estimate) is NOT established by this citation -- the only hard evidence is for a 0.3 km stub. This may simply mean GEM is tracking the intended eventual full-route repair using the first-phase approval as evidence of intent (reasonable), but it should be recorded as an inference, not as if the whole 68.93 km were documented. LengthKnownKm is correctly blank ('--').

fills.researcher_notes: DNR Minstroy Order 58-od (27.03.2025), OCR text read directly from the item's own djvu.txt derivative, repeatedly names this object 'magistralnogo gazoprovoda Mariupol-Berdyansk Du500' (main GAS pipeline) -- direct textual support for Fuel=Gas. Item page itself is live (url_verifier passes on '58-od' / '27.03.2025'); substring probes for Cyrillic 'gazoprovod'/'Berdyansk' fail against the bare details-page metadata (title/description only run a few words), which is expected for an archive.org item landing page -- I confirmed the actual content via the item's own full-text derivative, per url_verifier.py's documented content-false-negative guidance.

Same order explicitly calls this a 'magistralny gazoprovod' -- 'magistralny' = main/trunk transmission line (the standard Russian/Soviet technical term distinguishing trunk pipelines from distribution/gathering lines), supporting PipelineType=transmission (consistent with its parent P1457 original trunk and sibling P7817).

Order text names the object 'Mariupol-Berdyansk' verbatim, directly naming both endpoint cities. Oblast attribution (Donetsk / Zaporizhzhia) is standard geography, not separately sourced by this document.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Newest segment-specific evidence is the DNR Minstroy order (27.03.2025): planning documentation approved for a 0.3 km capital-repair stretch of Mariupol-Berdyansk -- i.e. still at the documentation/approval stage, not physical construction, consistent with Status=proposed. Independent (Ukrainian) corroboration that pipeline construction activity continues generally along this Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk-Melitopol corridor comes from united24media.com (24 Jul 2025, verified), though that article is about the corridor broadly and does not confirm or deny progress on the Mariupol-Berdyansk stretch specifically. Searched (RU/EN, Aug 2026) for any 2026 progress report specific to 'Mariupol-Berdyansk' capital repair / construction start -- found nothing newer than the 2025-03 order; TASS's 2024-04-29 piece on the 'Taganrog-Melitopol' modernization (P5989) discusses the DNR-side (Taganrog-Mariupol) segment and Zaporizhzhia-wide supply, not this specific Mariupol-Berdyansk stretch. Two Russian-origin items (the DNR order and the TASS/dan-news items on the neighboring corridor) count as ONE origin per the country brief; United24 is the second, independent origin, but it corroborates the corridor generally rather than this segment's exact status. Evidence age (~13-17 months as of Aug 2026) is well under the 2-year 'proposed with no progress' dormancy threshold, so 'confirm' rather than 'stale' is the right call -- but see the duplicate flag above: if P5989 is later found to already cover this exact stretch as 'operating,' this status would need revisiting as part of that adjudication, not as an independent status change here.

summary: P7818 (Mariupol-Berdyansk reconstruction, proposed, 500mm) is plausibly real but flagged twice: a duplicate/overlap concern against P5989 'Taganrog-Melitopol-Berdyansk Gas Pipeline' (recorded operating since 2024 on what may be the same corridor) needing cluster adjudication, and a spec/scope concern because the row's sole citation (DNR Minstroy Order 58-od) only documents planning approval for a 0.3 km repair stub, not the 68.93 km LengthEstimateKm on record. Filled Fuel/PipelineType/Location refs off that same primary document; status review verdict = confirm (newest independent evidence Jul 2025, well under the staleness threshold).
